_comment_family: Chelsea Market Pro ships as a single cut - a Regular, and the file in
fonts/ is it. Unlike the two Telegraf packs or the two Open Sans ones
there is no sibling here for a bare family name to be confused with,
so what gets declared is the file's own name ID 1 rather than a full
'Pro' is part of that name and not a decoration on it. There is a
plain 'Chelsea Market' out in the world, and a machine answering to
that name would be answering with some other file; the two are left as
two names for the same reason 'Telegraf' on its own is left out of the
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass. The face LOOKS
heavy - it is blocky hand lettering with thick, evenly weighted
strokes and flat-cut terminals - and asking for 700 on the strength of
how it looks would invite a browser to synthesise a bold on top of a
face that has no lighter cut to be bolder than.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name, which in this file is also the
Windows full name (name ID 4) - they are the same unspaced string,
where most faces here carry a spaced one for Windows and an unspaced
one for PostScript. It is what the installer registers the face under,
and Windows keys installed fonts by exactly that.
The second is the Mac full name, which in this file is the family name
over again. Listing it is safe here and would not be on most of these
packs: a family name matches every cut of a family, and this family
has one cut, so anything a machine hands back under it is this face.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied.
Impact and Arial Black, which most of this folder falls back through,
are absent for telegraf-ultralight's reason turned the other way up:
they are heavy grotesques, and this is hand lettering. A caption that
lost the file and came back in Impact would not read as the same brand
in a worse font, it would read as a different channel. Segoe Print and
Comic Sans MS are the nearest upright hands a Windows machine can be
relied on to have, and the generic `cursive` behind them is what CSS
has for a hand where those are gone too.
